'''Schwarzman Scholars''' ({{zh|s=苏世民学者|p=Sūshìmín Xuézhě}}), founded by American financier and philanthropist [[Stephen A. Schwarzman]], is a one-year fully-funded master's degree leadership program at [[Tsinghua University]] in [[Beijing]], [[China]].<ref name="program">{{cite web|title=Program|url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/program/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206152156/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/program|archive-date=6 December 2013|accessdate=4 December 2013|work=Schwarzman Scholars}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=8 February 2017|title=Steve Schwarzman Explains Why He Counsels Trump|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2017-02-08/steve-schwarzman-explains-why-he-counsels-trump|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170220004515/https://www.bloomberg.com/view/articles/2017-02-08/steve-schwarzman-explains-why-he-counsels-trump|archive-date=20 February 2017|access-date=23 February 2017|website=www.bloomberg.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=28 May 2020|title=Asia University Rankings|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2020/regional-ranking|access-date=4 December 2020|website=Times Higher Education (THE)|language=en|archive-date=4 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604055001/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/2020/regional-ranking|url-status=live}}</ref> The program selects 100–200 scholars per year based on their leadership ability, academic achievement, and commitment to advancing mutual cultural understanding and global progress.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Admissions |url=https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/ |access-date=4 December 2020 |website=Schwarzman Scholars |language=en-US |archive-date=28 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128043832/https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Selected scholars pursue a one-year master's degree in global affairs at Tsinghua University, residing at [[Schwarzman College]].<ref name=bradsher>{{cite news|last=Bradsher|first=Keith|title=$300 Million Scholarship for Study in China Signals a New Focus|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/21/world/asia/us-financier-backs-china-scholarship-program.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0|accessdate=4 December 2013|newspaper=The New York Times|date=20 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425085800/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/04/21/world/asia/us-financier-backs-china-scholarship-program.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0|archive-date=25 April 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

The program launched in June 2016, upon the completion of Schwarzman College at Tsinghua University, located in Beijing, China<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite web |url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/american-financier-stephen-a-schwarzman-endows-international-scholarship-program-in-china-2/ |title=Schwarzman Scholars » American Financier Stephen A. Schwarzman Endows International Scholarship Program in China |accessdate=31 January 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216225441/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/american-financier-stephen-a-schwarzman-endows-international-scholarship-program-in-china-2/ |archive-date=16 February 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=College |url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/college/ |work=Schwarzman Scholars |accessdate=4 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131130120950/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/college |archive-date=30 November 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> and is housed in a college designed by [[Robert A.M. Stern]], Dean of the [[Yale School of Architecture]]. It hosts up to 200 scholars annually from the United States, China, and other countries around the world. Schwarzman Scholars has an acceptance rate comparable to the [[Rhodes Scholarship|Rhodes]] and [[Marshall Scholarship|Marshall]] scholarships, making it one of the most competitive scholarships in the world.<ref>{{cite web|title=Beating the Odds to Become SMU's First Schwarzman Scholar|url=https://news.smu.edu.sg/news/2018/12/03/beating-odds-become-smus-first-schwarzman-scholar|access-date=11 May 2020|website=SMU Newsroom|date=3 December 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dartmouth students named Marshall, Schwarzman scholars|url=https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2020/01/dartmouth-students-named-marshall-schwarzman-scholars|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200112231259/https://www.thedartmouth.com/article/2020/01/dartmouth-students-named-marshall-schwarzman-scholars|archive-date=12 January 2020|access-date=11 May 2020|website=The Dartmouth}}</ref>

Modeled on the [[Rhodes Scholarship]] at [[Oxford University]] and the classical [[Academies (Shuyuan)|Chinese academies]] known as ''Shūyuàn'' (Schwarzman College is called ''Sūshìmín Shūyuàn'' in Chinese, translated directly as Schwarzman Academy), Schwarzman Scholars at Tsinghua University is a competitor in funding to similar international scholarship programs like the [[Yenching Scholarship]] at [[Peking University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bigstory.ap.org/article/2nd-chinese-university-starts-rhodes-style-program |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150118004248/http://bigstory.ap.org/article/2nd-chinese-university-starts-rhodes-style-program |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 January 2015 |title=2nd China university starts Rhodes-style program |date=5 May 2014 |accessdate=14 November 2018}}</ref> Since its founding, the program has maintained ties to the [[United Front Work Department]] as well as other organizations and personnel affiliated with the [[Chinese Communist Party]].<ref>{{cite January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/1231716/schwarzman-scholars-plan-raises-doubts-over-beijing|title=Schwarzman Scholars plan raises doubts January 2020}}</ref>

==History and motivation==
Schwarzman Scholars was conceptualized by its founder, [[Stephen A. Schwarzman]], in response to what he saw as growing [[China–United States relations|tensions between the United States and China]], largely due to China's economic growth.<ref name=":0" /> According to Schwarzman, in the fall of 2010, then-university president [[Gu Binglin]] asked if Schwarzman would want to help Tsinghua with a concept for a "Global Scholars" program. At the time, Schwarzman was on the advisory board of [[Tsinghua University]]'s [[Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management|School of Economics and Management]]. A year later in 2011, a delegation from Tsinghua visited Schwarzman in New York where the concept was put on hold until the leadership at Tsinghua had changed (the term of the then-executive administration was ending) and the [[2008 financial crisis]] had receded.<ref name=":0" />

In 2012, the newly appointed Tsinghua president [[Chen Jining]] met with Schwarzman in Paris. Schwarzman, who was interested in moving forward with the concept, put forth six ideas that would "reduce friction" for the new program. First, the college would need its own physical facility. Second, the program would need to be immersive, including travel and field work across the country with professors. Third, the program would assign mentors to each of the scholars in their area of interest. Fourth, there had to be no cost to the scholars. Fifth, the program would only be one year instead of two or three years long. Sixth and last, the program would be taught in English. Schwarzman told Chen: <blockquote>If we do this, what I really want to do is construct a program that has the same prestige as the Rhodes, because those are the students that I’m aiming for.<ref name=":0">{{Cite magazine|title=Rhodes East: Why Is the Schwarzman Scholarship in China?|url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/evan-osnos/rhodes-east-why-is-the-schwarzman-scholarship-in-china|last=Osnos|first=Evan|magazine=The New Yorker |date=26 April 2013|access-date=2020-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214084456/https://www.newyorker.com/news/evan-osnos/rhodes-east-why-is-the-schwarzman-scholarship-in-china|archive-date=2018-12-14|url-status=live}}</ref> </blockquote>With 200 scholars per year, he envisioned an alumni network of 10,000 scholars within a half century to include future heads of state and government.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.newyorker.com/news/evan-osnos/rhodes-east-why-is-the-schwarzman-scholarship-in-china|title=Rhodes East: Why Is the Schwarzman Scholarship in China?|magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=26 April 2013|access-date=1 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302030512/http://www.newyorker.com/news/evan-osnos/rhodes-east-why-is-the-schwarzman-scholarship-in-china|archive-date=2 March 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> In spring of 2013, the program was announced at the [[Great Hall of the People]], the seat of the [[National People's Congress]] in Beijing, China, and began its fundraising campaign.{{cn|date=December 2023}}

== Fundraising ==
In 2013, Stephen A. Schwarzman announced a $100 million personal gift and $200 million fundraising campaign to build and endow Schwarzman Scholars, an elite international scholarship program at Tsinghua University in Beijing.{{cn|date=December 2023}} Over $575 million has been raised to date, from a coterie of global donors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-06-19 |title=University announces unprecedented investment in the Humanities {{!}} University of Oxford |url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2019-06-19-university-announces-unprecedented-investment-humanities |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=www.ox.ac.uk |language=en |archive-date=24 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224211205/https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2019-06-19-university-announces-unprecedented-investment-humanities |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Stephen A. Schwarzman* |url=https://www.blackstone.com/people/stephen-a-schwarzman/ |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=Blackstone |language=en-US |archive-date=24 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224211205/https://www.blackstone.com/people/stephen-a-schwarzman/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Iyengar |first=Rishi |date=2019-06-19 |title=Stephen Schwarzman gives $188 million to Oxford to research AI ethics {{!}} CNN Business |url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/19/tech/stephen-schwarzman-oxford-ai-donation/index.html |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=CNN |language=en |archive-date=24 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240224211211/https://www.cnn.com/2019/06/19/tech/stephen-schwarzman-oxford-ai-donation/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oguh |first=Chibuike |date=September 9, 2020 |title=Blackstone's Schwarzman emerges as Wall Street's top political donor |website=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN2601N9/ |access-date=24 February 2024 |archive-date=20 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420221737/https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN2601N9/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In spring 2014, [[Peking University]], Tsinghua's chief rival, announced its own global scholarship program, the [[Yenching Scholars]] at [[Yenching Academy]], further increasing competition for funding. In summer 2014, Tsinghua University announced it had reached its original fundraising goal and that it would increase it to US$350 million. In 2014, when the program first launched its admissions process, Tsinghua's Schwarzman had already raised US$333&nbsp;million for its endowment fund. Shortly after a third target of US$400 million, to be reached by the following year, was announced. Commenting on the fundraising competition, Charles Conn, former warden of Rhodes House at Oxford University remarked:<blockquote>The Rhodes scholarships and Schwarzman Scholars programs have similar endowments and fund-raising goals. Which one is ahead in any given week depends mainly on the exchange rate of the pound, which has weakened lately against the dollar.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bradsher |first=Keith |date=2015-04-15 |title=During G.E. Deal, Blackstone's Schwarzman Focused on a Scholarship Fund |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/16/business/dealbook/despite-challenges-of-ge-deal-blackstones-schwarzman-kept-a-focus-on-scholar-program.html|access-date=2020-05-11|issn=0362-4331|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191027160719/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/16/business/dealbook/despite-challenges-of-ge-deal-blackstones-schwarzman-kept-a-focus-on-scholar-program.html|archive-date=2019-10-27|url-status=live}}</ref></blockquote>Meanwhile, it became clear that the Yenching Academy at Peking University would be funded through Chinese private donations and government grants, which set off competition to further grow the two programs' endowments. As a result of the increased competition among full-scholarship leadership programs, there was a marked growth in fundraising, with the endowments moving towards a half billion USD each.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/news/announcement |title=Rhodes Scholarships receive landmark £75 million donation from McCall MacBain Foundation - the Rhodes Scholarships |access-date=1 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170226104848/http://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/news/announcement |archive-date=26 February 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="ReferenceA" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://english.pku.edu.cn/News_Events/News/Focus/11335.htm |title=Yenching Academy: Elite China experience for future global leaders_Peking University |access-date=1 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314040916/http://english.pku.edu.cn/News_Events/News/Focus/11335.htm |archive-date=14 March 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-endowment-achieves-300-million-fundraising-milestone/|title=Schwarzman Scholars|access-date=1 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221171400/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-endowment-achieves-300-million-fundraising-milestone/|archive-date=21 February 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/16/business/dealbook/despite-challenges-of-ge-deal-blackstones-schwarzman-kept-a-focus-on-scholar-program.html|title=During G.E. Deal,&nbsp;Blackstone's Schwarzman Focused on a Scholarship Fund|work=The New York Times |date=15 April 2015 |access-date=1 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170719164158/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/04/16/business/dealbook/despite-challenges-of-ge-deal-blackstones-schwarzman-kept-a-focus-on-scholar-program.html|archive-date=19 July 2017|url-status=live |last1=Bradsher |first1=Keith }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ioe.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/ioe/5331/20141017140314673966581/Perils%20of%20Academic%20Competition,%20Past%20and%20Present%20-%20.pdf |title=Academic competition results |website=www.ioe.tsinghua.edu.cn |access-date=1 March 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303221837/http://www.ioe.tsinghua.edu.cn/publish/ioe/5331/20141017140314673966581/Perils%20of%20Academic%20Competition,%20Past%20and%20Present%20-%20.pdf |archive-date=3 March 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Program design and allocation==
Schwarzman Scholars study for a one-year master's degree (Master of Management Science; Chinese: 管理科学硕士<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sc.tsinghua.edu.cn/newsletter/798.jhtml|title=人民日报 {{!}} 清华有个苏世民书院|access-date=26 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426131633/http://www.sc.tsinghua.edu.cn/newsletter/798.jhtml|archive-date=26 April 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>) in Global Affairs<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/faq/|title=FAQ|access-date=26 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417041501/https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/faq/|archive-date=17 April 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> (Chinese: 全球领导力<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_1541243|title=清华大学苏世民书院如何培养未来世界领导者？|access-date=26 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190426125024/https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_1541243|archive-date=26 April 2019|url-status=live}}</ref>) at [[Tsinghua University]]. The required core curriculum centers on three pillars: Leadership, Global Affairs, and China. The scholars live and study at the [[Schwarzman College]], a purpose-built residential college inside Tsinghua University designed by [[Robert A.M. Stern]], former Dean of the [[Yale School of Architecture]].<ref name="bradsher" /> Scholars live in Beijing for a year of study.

Approximately 40% of the participants come from the U.S., 20% from China and 40% from the rest of the world. Students apply directly to the program and are not required to obtain a nomination from their university. The [[Institute of International Education]] in the U.S., which administers the [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright Scholarships]], was initially responsible for the international and American selection processes. This process is now managed by the program's Admissions team.<ref name="schwarzmanscholars.org">{{cite web|url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/|title=Schwarzman Scholars|access-date=2 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150131230832/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/|archive-date=31 January 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Prospective applicants with passports and permanent resident cards from [[Mainland China]], Hong Kong, [[Macau]], and [[Taiwan]], are required to apply earlier than applicants from other countries using a different online application portal, regardless of where they may have attended university or reside.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Schwarzman Scholars|url=https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/application/|access-date=18 October 2020|website=Schwarzman Scholars|archive-date=7 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201007023128/https://www.schwarzmanscholars.org/admissions/application/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Cohorts==
The program is based on a cohort system, where admitted students live, dine and study together in a close environment, similar to the [[Collegiate university|collegiate system]] in some British Universities. In 2014, Schwarzman Scholars held four recruitment launch events in New York City (at the Morgan Library & Museum), Singapore (introduced by [[National University of Singapore]] President [[Tan Chorh Chuan|Tan Chor Chuan]]), London (at the [[Tower Bridge]], introduced by [[Oxford University]] Vice-Chancellor [[Andrew D. Hamilton]]), and [[Palo Alto]] in the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] (at [[Stanford University]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launches-recruitment-efforts/|title=Schwarzman Scholars|access-date=16 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221210213/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launches-recruitment-efforts/|archive-date=21 February 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launch-event-in-singapore/|title=Schwarzman Scholars|access-date=16 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221153646/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launch-event-in-singapore/|archive-date=21 February 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launch-event-in-london/|title=Schwarzman Scholars|access-date=16 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206003210/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/schwarzman-scholars-launch-event-in-london/|archive-date=6 February 2015|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://schwarzmanscholars.org/blackstone-ceo-stumps-at-stanford-for-his-scholarship-program-2/ |title=Schwarzman Scholars » Blackstone CEO stumps at Stanford for his scholarship program |accessdate=16 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150216183545/http://schwarzmanscholars.org/blackstone-ceo-stumps-at-stanford-for-his-scholarship-program-2/ |archive-date=16 February 2015}}</ref>

The inaugural cohort of 111 scholars was announced on January 10, 2016, and selected from a group of roughly 3,050 applicants.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/11/business/dealbook/schwarzman-scholars-announces-inaugural-class-to-study-in-china.html?_r=0|title=Schwarzman Scholars Announces Inaugural Class to Study in China|work=The New York Times |date=11 January 2016 |access-date=23 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305114700/http://www.nytimes.com/2016/01/11/business/dealbook/schwarzman-scholars-announces-inaugural-class-to-study-in-china.html?_r=0|archive-date=5 five graduates of [[Princeton University|Princeton]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dailyprincetonian.com/news/2016/01/2-undergraduates-3-alumni-selected-as-schwarzman-scholars/|title=2 undergraduates, 3 Schwarzman Scholars|date=16 January 2016|access-date=18 January ==Leadership and governance==
===International advisory board===
* The Right Honorable [[Tony Blair]], former prime minister of the United Kingdom (honorary)
* The Right Honorable [[Brian Mulroney]], former prime minister of Canada (honorary)
* The Honorable [[Kevin Rudd]], former prime minister of Australia (honorary)
* [[Henry Paulson|Henry "Hank" Paulson]], 74th [[United States Secretary of the Treasury]] (honorary)
* [[John L. Thornton]], chairman of the [[Brookings Institution]], professor and director of Global Leadership at Tsinghua University (honorary)
* [[Condoleezza Rice]], 66th United States Secretary of State (honorary)

===Academic advisory council===
Schwarzman Scholars has an [[Advisory Board|advisory board]] whose members include former leaders in government and affiliates of institutions such as [[Harvard]], [[Yale]], [[Stanford]], [[Duke]] and [[Oxford]].

* Qian Yingyi, Distinguished Professor of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Tsinghua University; Former Dean, School of Economics and Management, Tsinghua University
